candidates.hypothesis: Exponential moving average of observed states. At observed steps, memory blends the new sync with older memory; at unobserved steps, memory is recomputed from the same unchanged inputs and gradually converges toward last_sync. The intent is to smooth noisy oscillations in hidden activations while weighting recent observations more heavily than the fixed 50/50 average does.
candidates.falsifier: Final-two-cycle accuracy is at or below the frozen averaging comparator on development seeds. A second failure condition is that the estimate's error at age 1 exceeds the comparator's, which would show the early bias from older memory dominates.

candidates.hypothesis: Constant small trend step, stateless. The prediction adds a quarter of the last inter-observation difference to last_sync and does not depend on age. This is a conservative momentum guess that avoids over-extrapolating over a 16-epoch gap, as an alternative to averaging, which lags behind the trend.
candidates.falsifier: Development-seed accuracy over the final two cycles does not exceed the frozen average. Another failure sign is that the difference between consecutive syncs is uncorrelated with the subsequent change, which would make the added term pure noise.

candidates.hypothesis: Per-node norm-growth scaling: memory stores the clipped relative change in each node's activation norm between the last two syncs. The prediction rescales last_sync by one plus that rate, preserving direction while tracking the growth or shrinkage of activation magnitude during training. Clipping to ±0.2 bounds the risk of overshooting.
candidates.falsifier: Final-two-cycle mean accuracy on development seeds is not above the frozen averaging comparator. It also fails if node norms do not change persistently across cycles, in which case the rescaling adds error without benefit.

candidates.hypothesis: This estimator continues the inter-observation change conservatively. It adds at most half of the last observed change, scaled by the fraction of the gap elapsed. The added change is never more than the last change itself. This should cover part of the true drift during late training, when changes shrink, while staying close to hold.
candidates.falsifier: Final-seed mean accuracy over the final two cycles is not higher than the frozen two-point-average comparator. Alternatively, it is indistinguishable from or worse than hold.

candidates.hypothesis: Memory keeps an EMA level of the observed states, updated only at observations. The gap between the last observation and this smoothed level gives a lower-noise drift direction than a single two-point difference. A small fraction of that gap is added, ramped over the interval. This resembles a baseline-plus-damped-trend predictor.
candidates.falsifier: Final-seed mean accuracy over the last two synchronization cycles is not above the frozen two-point-average comparator. Alternatively, it is below hold.

candidates.hypothesis: Damped linear-trend extrapolation, inspired by the SNI-style trend term. The per-epoch slope (last_sync - previous_sync)/observed_interval is projected forward with a scaled-down horizon (age/4). A tanh(4/(age+1)) factor shrinks the projection as age grows. If hidden states drift smoothly during training, this should track them better than the two-sync average. The two-sync average lags behind by half an interval, so trend-following may raise exact-forward accuracy in the final cycles. Memory is unused.
candidates.falsifier: On development seeds, mean exact-forward accuracy over the final two synchronization cycles is not higher than the frozen two-sync-average comparator, or is lower than hold.

candidates.hypothesis: Shrinks the last sync slightly toward a long-run EMA of observed states. This acts as a variance-reduction estimator: if late-training hidden states fluctuate around a stable mean, a light shrink can reduce error. Its weight on last_sync is heavier than the comparator's 0.5, which limits lag. It serves as a conservative alternative to the trend-based candidates.
candidates.falsifier: Mean final-two-cycle accuracy is at or below the two-sync-average comparator on development seeds, or is indistinguishable from hold.

candidates.hypothesis: Hidden states drift mostly monotonically under constant-rate Adam. A damped linear extrapolation tracks that drift better than the backward-looking average. The extrapolation uses half the inter-sync difference, scaled by the elapsed fraction of the interval and capped at one interval. The cap limits overshoot in the first stale cycle, where the observed interval is 1. ReLU keeps the estimate in the post-ReLU range.
candidates.falsifier: Development seeds show that mean exact-forward accuracy over the final two sync cycles is not above the two-sync average comparator. Alternatively, per-layer estimation error versus later observed states is larger than that of the average comparator.

candidates.hypothesis: Memory keeps an exponential moving average of the per-epoch velocity normalized by the observed interval, which smooths noisy differences across syncs. The prediction adds a damped, age-capped velocity step to the last sync. This should reduce staleness relative to averaging while avoiding large extrapolation.
candidates.falsifier: Development seeds show final-two-cycle mean accuracy at or below the average comparator. Alternatively, removing the velocity term so that the program reduces to hold performs equally well or better.

candidates.hypothesis: The 50/50 average leans too heavily on an older state that is 16 epochs stale. Weighting the latest sync at 0.75 keeps some noise smoothing while reducing that bias. The estimate is a convex combination of nonnegative states, so it is stable and nonnegative.
candidates.falsifier: Development-seed final-two-cycle mean accuracy does not exceed the average comparator. Alternatively, the estimate does not lie between hold and the average comparator in measured estimation error.

candidates.hypothesis: Memory acts as a per-epoch exponential moving average of last_sync. It converges toward the latest sync during stale epochs while retaining a little older history right after a sync. A small blend toward this smoothed anchor regularizes feature noise with less staleness bias than the two-sync average.
candidates.falsifier: Development seeds show final-two-cycle mean accuracy at or below the average comparator, or no improvement over hold.

candidates.hypothesis: The extrapolation fraction saturates: tanh(age/interval) is below 1, so the predicted displacement never exceeds one full observed difference. Over the 16-epoch interval, the prediction ramps toward a fraction of the last inter-sync change. This bounds the risk of overshoot while still advancing the state beyond hold.
candidates.falsifier: On development seeds, final two-cycle accuracy is not above the two-sync averaging comparator. Alternatively, estimation error late in each cycle (age 10 to 15) is larger than under hold.
